skill.name: async-sync-advisor
skill.description: Advises on async, sync, and mixed concurrency patterns for Rust AWS Lambda handlers using tokio, spawn_blocking, and rayon.
skill.summary: Choose the right async or sync pattern for Rust AWS Lambda workloads.
skill.author: EmilLindfors

content.value_statement: Rust Lambda handlers often mix I/O and CPU work, which can block runtimes or waste parallelism. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward clear async, blocking, and Rayon patterns.
actual_capabilities: Identifies whether a Rust Lambda workload is I/O-bound, CPU-bound, or mixed.
Recommends tokio async patterns for independent network, database, and storage operations.
Suggests spawn_blocking when CPU-intensive work would block the async runtime.
Shows when Rayon can parallelize CPU-bound collection processing.
Explains common mistakes such as sequential I/O and CPU work inside async handlers.
limitations: Does not run benchmarks, profilers, or load tests.
Focuses on Rust AWS Lambda handlers, not every Rust concurrency use case.
Does not provide complete production error handling or infrastructure configuration.
Assumes tokio, futures, and Rayon are acceptable dependencies for the project.

use_cases.title: Review a New Lambda Handler
use_cases.description: Check whether a new Rust Lambda handler should use async I/O, blocking work, or both.

use_cases.title: Improve Lambda Performance
use_cases.description: Find places where sequential awaits or CPU work may reduce throughput.

use_cases.title: Teach Concurrency Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Explain when tokio, spawn_blocking, and Rayon fit different Lambda workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Classify My Handler
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one Lambda function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust Lambda handler. Tell me whether the workload is I/O-bound, CPU-bound, or mixed, and suggest the best concurrency pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Blocking Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Find CPU-intensive work in this async Rust Lambda handler. Suggest where spawn_blocking should be used and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Parallelize Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Lambda handler that processes many items. Decide whether Rayon is appropriate, and describe how to combine it with async I/O safely.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Mixed Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture for download, transform, and upload flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Rust Lambda concurrency plan for downloading records, processing them, and uploading results. Separate async phases from blocking or parallel phases.

output_examples.input: A handler fetches user, profile, and settings one after another.
output_examples.output: The response recommends concurrent async I/O because the calls are independent. It explains that waiting sequentially increases latency without improving correctness.

output_examples.input: A handler hashes a large payload inside an async function.
output_examples.output: The response recommends moving the hash computation to a blocking thread. It explains that CPU-heavy work can stall the async runtime.

output_examples.input: A handler downloads many files, transforms them, and uploads results.
output_examples.output: The response separates the workflow into async download, blocking parallel transform, and async upload phases. It explains where Rayon may help.

best_practices: Classify each handler phase as I/O-bound, CPU-bound, or mixed before choosing a pattern.
Use async joins for independent I/O operations that can safely run concurrently.
Move CPU-heavy work away from the async runtime with spawn_blocking or a parallel worker pattern.
anti_patterns: Do not make CPU-heavy work async only because it runs inside an async handler.
Do not await independent I/O calls sequentially when their order is not required.
Do not add Rayon to small workloads without checking overhead and Lambda CPU limits.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and example patterns for Rust Lambda handlers.

faq.question: When should I use async in Lambda?
faq.answer: Use async for network, database, storage, and other I/O operations that spend time waiting.

faq.question: When should I use spawn_blocking?
faq.answer: Use spawn_blocking for CPU-intensive or blocking work that would otherwise stall the async runtime.

faq.question: When is Rayon useful?
faq.answer: Rayon is useful for large CPU-bound collections that can be processed in parallel.

faq.question: Can it replace benchmarking?
faq.answer: No. It gives design guidance, but benchmarks are still needed for final performance decisions.

faq.question: Does it support non-Rust Lambda functions?
faq.answer: No. The guidance is written for Rust Lambda handlers using tokio and related Rust libraries.
